preamble: The thematic answers are all birds. A thematic clue may have no definition; where one has a definition, it is not a thematic one.

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: torn letters are ripped apart and scattered

explanation.surface: A communist insurgent in a country ripped apart by fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: This puzzle is themed on birds: many answers, this one included, have no definition in the clue, and the theme stands in for it. The hyphen in 'war-torn' hides that 'war' is fodder and 'torn' the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed warbler is a small brown songbird of reed beds, one of the puzzle's unclued birds.

clue.text: Go up into allotment before Ascension Day

definitions.note: The definition is a description of when the Rogation days fall rather than a synonym; ROGATION is used as a modifier, as in Rogation Sunday.

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending GO up writes it bottom to top

parts.note: a ration is an allotment, a fixed share; OG goes inside it after the R

explanation.surface: An instruction to climb onto your allotment plot before a church feast day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go up' reads as a phrasal verb; it splits into GO plus a reversal instruction, which works because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rogation days are the three days of prayer immediately before Ascension Day in the Christian calendar.

parts.note: the surface reading: crying, water from the eyes
the setter's reading: a medicine applied in drops to the eye, which is what tears literally are

explanation.walkthrough: Tears are read literally as drops coming from the eye; the question mark flags that the answer is really the medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Tears are drops of liquid from the eye, which is a playful reading of 'eyedrops', the medicine.

clue.text: Former naval officers run in all directions

parts.note: the four compass points W, E, N, S; R goes in after W

explanation.surface: Ex-navy officers scattering every which way.
explanation.walkthrough: Wrens were members of the Women's Royal Naval Service (WRNS), the British women's navy until 1993. The answer is also a bird, fitting the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrens were members of the Women's Royal Naval Service, disbanded as a separate service in 1993, so 'former'.

clue.text: Transported by the middle of the floorshow

parts.note: rapt = transported, carried away with delight

indicators.note: keep the three central letters of 'floorshow'

parts.note: the middle three of the nine letters: flo-ORS-how

explanation.surface: Someone enraptured by the centrepiece of a cabaret.
explanation.walkthrough: Another unclued bird: raptors are birds of prey. The 'middle' here is three letters, not one.
explanation.definitionFit: Raptors are birds of prey such as hawks and eagles, part of the puzzle's bird theme.

indicators.note: the letters are not in their proper form

explanation.surface: A shop sign offering seconds: shoes with slight flaws going cheap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For sale' reads as a shop sign; it is the fodder, and 'imperfect' tells you to rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: loafers are one kind of shoe, a slip-on style with no laces.

parts.note: the stern is the rear of a ship
a guard travels on a train

explanation.surface: A severe railway worker's way of protecting himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' looks like an adjective describing the employee; it is the noun, the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearguard is a defence, especially one mounted at the back of a retreating force.

indicators.note: the answer sits in the following words

parts.note: the answer runs across the gap, from the end of 'the' into the start of 'nude'

explanation.surface: A reveller at a party with no clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen party is a British bride-to-be's night out with her friends, so a hen is one who goes to it. The answer is also a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen is a woman attending a hen party, the celebration before a wedding.

parts.note: split into HOUSE and WORK: HO is the abbreviation for house, OP (opus) a work

indicators.note: take the outside letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone told to take the chores out into the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Housework' must be split into HOUSE and WORK. The first 'outside' is the instruction and the second is the word it acts on. The hoopoe is an unclued bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoopoe is a crested pinkish bird with barred wings, part of the puzzle's bird theme.

clue.text: Two journalists from the north-east required

explanation.surface: A newspaper needs two reporters sent down from the north-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: ED for editor is the standard crossword journalist; two of them follow NE, the compass abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Needed and required both mean necessary.

indicators.note: something seen regularly turns up at even intervals, so the answer is every other letter of the words

parts.note: G-a-R-d-E-n-B-e-E-s: first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: Someone startled to find bees in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: An unclued bird: the grebe is a diving waterbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The grebe is a diving waterbird, part of the puzzle's bird theme.

parts.note: the stammered P stands as a letter on its own
Prince Hal, the young Henry V in Shakespeare
the rope is one of the six weapons in the board game Cluedo (Clue in the US)

explanation.surface: A stammered accusation in Cluedo: the Prince did it, with a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter is not decoration: it supplies the opening P. The phalarope is an unclued wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The phalarope is a small wading bird, part of the puzzle's bird theme.

parts.note: a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: Something going red, or pale, or green.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a definition of 'turns', but it is all wordplay; the turnstone is an unclued shore bird that flips stones for food.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnstone is a shore bird that turns over stones to find food, part of the puzzle's bird theme.

parts.note: the Home Counties are the counties round London, in the south-east (SE) of England

explanation.surface: A trip around the counties surrounding London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a preposition governing the Home Counties; it is the letter O. The goose is an unclued bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The goose is a large waterbird, part of the puzzle's bird theme.

indicators.note: what you hear, not what is written

parts.note: OS = Ordnance Survey, Britain's national mapmakers; praise = acclamation

explanation.surface: Mapmakers being applauded, loudly enough to be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ordnance Survey (OS) is Britain's official mapping agency. Ospreys are unclued fish-eating birds of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: Ospreys are fish-eating birds of prey, part of the puzzle's bird theme.

clue.text: Genial men resorted to coating fired on metal in the US

definitions.text: coating fired on metal in the US

indicators.note: re-sorted: the letters sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: Friendly men turning to a metalwork craft on their American holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resorted to' reads as 'turned to'; split it as re-sorted. 'In the US' justifies the single L; British spelling is enamelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Enameling, in American spelling, is fusing a glassy coating onto metal by firing it.

parts.note: S = small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Getting a pound coin out of a little witch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quid' is not the British slang for a pound: it is a wad of chewing tobacco, and shag is coarse-cut tobacco. The shag is also a bird, a kind of cormorant.
explanation.definitionFit: Shag is coarse tobacco, and a quid is a lump of tobacco for chewing, so a quid might be made of shag.

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone pleading with the person arranging a recording session to relent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do give in' reads as a plea to surrender; it is the fodder, with 'organising' as the instruction to rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: making a video of something is one way of recording it.

clue.text: A dilettante — he's taken in by fancy tea-set

indicators.note: HE is taken inside the rearranged letters
the letters are made fancy, rearranged

parts.note: TEASET rearranged, split into AEST and TE
the word he, taken as it stands and placed between the two halves

explanation.surface: An idle dabbler in the arts, seduced by an ornate tea service.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'he's taken in by' as 'he is taken in by': HE sits inside the jumbled TEA-SET. 'Fancy' is the anagram indicator, fancy meaning elaborate, not liking.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete cultivates a love of beauty and the arts, often shallowly, as a dilettante does.

clue.text: Track from the west of Cagliari

indicators.note: the answer is taken from inside the next word
read towards the west, right to left

explanation.surface: A route out of the western side of Cagliari, the Sardinian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The west of' sounds like a location in Sardinia; in an across clue it means read westward. Rail is both a track and an unclued bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail is a track, as in a railway line; the rail is also a marsh bird.

clue.text: Part of the stumps I. Bell replaced with silver

indicators.note: the letters are placed again in a new order

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Ian Bell, the England batsman, putting the stumps back after being bowled.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the stumps are topped by two bails; the leg bail is the one on the batsman's leg side. Ian Bell played cricket for England.
explanation.definitionFit: The leg bail is the bail resting on the leg-side stumps of the wicket.

parts.note: kite is old RAF slang for an aeroplane

explanation.surface: A 'stop' marking painted on a Royal Air Force plane.
explanation.walkthrough: The red kite is an unclued bird of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: The red kite is a fork-tailed bird of prey, part of the puzzle's bird theme.

clue.text: Lessen intensity of real life events, all getting half-cut

indicators.note: each word loses half of its letters, keeping the front half

explanation.surface: Taking the edge off real-life dramas when everyone involved is drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-cut is British slang for tipsy, which is the surface meaning; the cryptic reading cuts each word in half.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to relieve pain or pressure is to ease it, lowering how strongly it is felt.

explanation.surface: A financier has gone bust, and serves him right.
explanation.walkthrough: BROKE is the everyday word for having no money; R for right is standard.
explanation.definitionFit: A broker deals in stocks or other financial products on behalf of clients.

clue.text: Feverish fellow caught twice admitting sex is over

indicators.note: something that is over has been turned over, so IT is flipped end to end

parts.note: it = sex (old slang), turned over; it goes between the two Cs

explanation.surface: A sweaty man arrested twice, confessing an affair has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex is over' reads as the end of a fling, but 'is over' is the reversal instruction. IT for sex is an old convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Hectic once meant feverish, as in a hectic flush, the flushed cheeks of a fever.

clue.text: Change course back to Edgbaston, first

indicators.note: VEER is written backwards
take the first letter of Edgbaston

parts.note: the first letter of EDGBASTON, a cricket ground in Birmingham

explanation.surface: A driver doubling back towards Edgbaston, the Birmingham cricket ground, as a priority.
explanation.walkthrough: The reeve is the female of the ruff, a wading bird, so this is another unclued member of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve is a female ruff, a wading bird, part of the puzzle's bird theme.

clue.text: Scored goal — not centre — curling to back of net

indicators.note: GOAL loses its middle letters OA
take the last letter of 'net'
the letters curl round into a new order

explanation.surface: A football report: a goal scored off-centre, with the shot bending into the back of the net.
explanation.walkthrough: Everything here is football, so 'curling' reads as a bending shot; it is the anagram indicator. The goldcrest, Britain's smallest bird, is unclued.
explanation.definitionFit: The goldcrest is a tiny songbird with a gold crown stripe, part of the puzzle's bird theme.

explanation.surface: A blameless husband drops out of his course at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' looks like a school lesson the husband walks out of; it is the definition, a social rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a caste is a hereditary social rank, originally in the Hindu system, so a class in the social sense.

clue.text: Pool, we hear, has to stir

indicators.note: what is heard, not written

parts.note: a kitty is a shared pool of money
to wake = to stir from sleep

explanation.surface: A remark that a swimming pool needs mixing.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the KITTY part is a sound-alike, so the spelling KITTI is fair. The kittiwake is an unclued gull.
explanation.definitionFit: The kittiwake is a small cliff-nesting gull, part of the puzzle's bird theme.

indicators.note: PIE is broken up and rearranged

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

explanation.surface: A pie tin, dropped and broken, as the first thing that went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'pie-tin' glues together two separate pieces. The snipe is an unclued long-billed wader.
explanation.definitionFit: The snipe is a long-billed wading bird, part of the puzzle's bird theme.

clue.text: It's said to be steady — and unsteady!

indicators.note: it sounds like, when said

parts.note: a rock is steady (solid as a rock), and to rock is to sway unsteadily

explanation.surface: A paradox: something both firm and wobbly at once.
explanation.walkthrough: ROCK means both opposites, and ROC sounds the same. The roc is the giant bird of Arabian legend, unclued like the other birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is an enormous mythical bird from the Arabian Nights, part of the puzzle's bird theme.

indicators.note: the letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A news report on a missing plane that is said to have come down.
explanation.walkthrough: The golden eagle, a large bird of prey, completes the unclued birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden eagle is a large brown bird of prey, part of the puzzle's bird theme.
